current: DECLAN MOTH is Declan Twomey, a Cork-born baritone who has spent ten years working nights in Toronto — first driving a bakery van at 2 a.m., now running the overnight desk at a small community radio station. As a boy who wouldn't sleep, he rode along on his grandfather's late drives around Cork's ring road, a box of cassettes taped off late-night radio at his feet; when his grandfather died, those 43 tapes crossed the Atlantic in a shoebox, and their hiss is still in every mix. His songs are slow, warm synthwave for the stretch between last call and first light: analog pads, a gated snare, a voice that sounds like it's riding in the passenger seat, and always a time on the clock. Put it on when you're driving home and everyone else is asleep.
